tldr: Oregon Public Universities submitted this advocacy presentation arguing they deliver on state goals and generate significant economic return: $10 billion annually with 30,000+ employees, a $10 return for every $1 of state investment, and 85% of income taxes from degree-holders. They contend higher education is essential for future workforce (72% of 2031 jobs will require postsecondary education) while highlighting rising costs, particularly operational expenses outpacing inflation and revenue.

bullets.text: $10 billion+ in annual economic impact; 30,000+ employees in Oregon; nearly 500,000 alumni
Return on investment: $1 state investment generates $10 in economic impact
85% of income taxes paid by those with a bachelor's degree or higher
By 2031, 72% of US jobs will require postsecondary education and/or training
State appropriation per FTE: $626.2 million; Net tuition per FTE: $551.63 million
Nearly 80% of university costs directed toward personnel
OPE (operational/post-secondary education) costs rising faster than inflation and revenue
